definition_en: the row of bones down the back, the narrow back edge of a book, or a sharp point on a plant or an animal
core_image: 沿着后背排开的一串尖突骨节
scene: 体检时，医生用手指沿着病人的后背正中往下按，一节一节地数。The doctor ran a finger down the middle of the back and counted each bone of the spine.
sceneCN: 这里 spine 是「脊柱」（第 1 个义项：后背正中那一列椎骨）；句意：体检时，医生用手指沿着后背正中往下按，一节一节数出脊柱的骨头。

derivatives.zh: 脊柱的；由 spine 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，义为与脊柱有关的
无脊椎的；懦弱的；由 spine 加否定词尾 -less 构成
多刺的；由 spine 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，形容长满尖刺

senses.title: The backbone
senses.definition: the row of bones that runs down the back and holds the body upright
senses.definitionCN: 沿后背排列、把身体撑直的一列骨头
senses.example: A fall from the ladder damaged his spine.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，伤了脊柱。
senses.why: Latin spina first named a thorn and then the backbone, because the vertebrae stand out under the skin like a row of small points.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 spina 先指一根刺，再指脊柱，因为一节节椎骨隔着皮肤凸起，就像一排小尖点。

senses.title: The back of a book
senses.definition: the narrow back edge of a book, where the pages are joined together
senses.definitionCN: 书本背面那条窄边，书页在这里被装订在一起
senses.example: The title is printed along the book spine.
senses.why: A book spine holds the pages together the way a backbone holds a body, so the same word was borrowed for that narrow edge.
senses.whyCN: 书脊把书页撑在一起，正像脊柱把身体撑起来，于是同一个词被借去指那条窄边。

senses.title: A sharp point
senses.definition: a thin sharp point on a plant or an animal, such as a thorn or a quill
senses.definitionCN: 植物或动物身上细而尖的突起，如荆棘的刺或动物的棘
senses.example: The cactus spines can pierce a thick glove.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人掌的刺能扎穿厚手套。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of spina, a prickle or thorn, and it is the sharp point from which the whole word family grew.
senses.whyCN: 这是 spina 最古老的含义：一根刺、一个尖点，也是整个词族生长出来的起点。

senses.title: Main support or courage
senses.definition: the central support of a group or thing, or the courage to face a hard situation
senses.definitionCN: 某个团体或事物的核心支撑，也指面对困境时的勇气
senses.example: She showed real spine when she refused the unsafe plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒绝那个不安全的方案时，表现出真正的骨气。
senses.why: If the backbone keeps a body upright, then spine can name whatever keeps a group or a person standing.
senses.whyCN: 既然脊柱让身体挺直，spine 也就能够指让一个团体或一个人挺住的东西。

intro.en: Spine comes from Latin spina, a thorn or prickle that also named the backbone, and reached English through Old French espine.
intro.cn: spine 来自拉丁语 spina（刺、棘，也指脊柱），经古法语 espine 进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root, usually written as spei, carried the idea of a sharp point.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根，通常写作 spei，带有「尖点」的意思。

items.en: Spina means a thorn or prickle, and also the backbone of a person or an animal.
items.cn: spina 指刺、棘，也指人或动物的脊柱。

items.en: Anatomists wrote spina dorsi for the spine of the back.
items.cn: 解剖学著作写作 spina dorsi，指背部的脊柱。

items.en: Espine carries the thorn sense into French.
items.cn: espine 把「刺」的含义带进法语。

items.en: Spine appears in English with both the thorn sense and the backbone sense.
items.cn: 中古英语的 spine 同时带有「刺」与「脊柱」两个含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the book spine and the figurative sense of courage or support.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上「书脊」以及「骨气、支柱」的引申义。

note.en: Spine belongs to a Latin family of sharp-point words, and in meaning it stands near backbone, thorn, and vertebra.
note.cn: spine 属于拉丁语中表示「尖点」的词族，在意义上靠近 backbone、thorn 与 vertebra。

entries.definitionCN: 快速旋转；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the row of bones down the back
a sharp point on a plant
one single bone of the spine
entries.definitionCN: 椎骨；脊柱上的一块骨头

normalIntro.en: Spine is the sharp point that turned into a backbone: Latin spina named a thorn first and the back bones second.
normalIntro.cn: spine 是由「尖点」变成的「脊柱」：拉丁语 spina 先指刺，后指背上的骨头。

normal.en: Latin spina means both a thorn and the backbone, because the vertebrae feel like a row of small thorns under the skin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 spina 既指刺也指脊柱，因为隔着皮肤摸椎骨，就像摸到一排小刺。

normal.en: The book spine is the back of the book, named after the backbone it resembles.
normal.cn: 书脊是书的背面，得名于它像脊柱一样把整体撑住。

normal.en: A spine injury is a damaged backbone, common after a hard fall.
normal.cn: spine injury 是脊柱受伤，重重摔一跤之后很常见。

normal.en: Spinal is the adjective: spinal cord, spinal nerve, spinal column.
normal.cn: spinal 是形容词：spinal cord 脊髓、spinal nerve 脊神经、spinal column 脊柱。

normal.en: Compare thorn: a thorn is a point on a plant, while spine covers plants, animals, the backbone, and a book.
normal.cn: 对比 thorn：thorn 专指植物的刺，spine 则覆盖植物、动物、脊柱与书脊。

abstract.en: Picture your hand running down the middle of a back and finding a row of small knobs.
abstract.cn: 想象手掌沿着后背正中往下滑，摸到一排凸起的小骨节。

abstract.en: Picture a closed book standing upright, its narrow back facing you like a straight spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一本合上的书立起来，窄窄的书脊朝向你，像一根笔直的脊柱。

abstract.en: Picture a cactus pad with one thin needle just touching a fingertip.
abstract.cn: 想象仙人掌的一片掌上，一根细针正碰到指尖。

examples.en: He injured his spine in a fall from the ladder.
examples.cn: 他从梯子上摔下来，伤了脊柱。

examples.en: The book spine was cracked and the pages came loose.
examples.cn: 那本书的书脊裂了，书页松脱下来。

examples.en: Cactus spines keep animals from eating the plant.
examples.cn: 仙人掌的刺让动物没法啃食这株植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「死拼」——拼到脊柱都伤了；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语 spina 无关。

root: 拉丁语 spina（刺、棘，也指脊柱）→ 古法语 espine（刺）→ 中古英语 spine → 现代英语 spine；核心义是「尖起的骨节」，由刺扩展到脊柱、书脊与骨气。

sensesIntro.en: Spine starts from the sharp point named by Latin spina, then covers the backbone, the back of a book, and finally the idea of support or courage.
sensesIntro.cn: spine 从拉丁语 spina 的「尖刺」出发，先指脊柱，再指书脊，最后引申为支撑与骨气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of small sharp knobs standing along the back.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿着后背排开的一串小小尖突。

branches.en: The backbone is the anatomical core of the word.
branches.cn: 脊柱是这个词在解剖学上的核心义。

branches.en: The book spine borrows the shape of a backbone.
branches.cn: 书脊义借用了脊柱的形状。

branches.en: The sharp point is the oldest sense of the Latin source.
branches.cn: 尖刺义是拉丁语来源中最古老的义项。

branches.en: A backbone is literally a row of pointed bones, so the two senses share one shape.
branches.cn: 脊柱本来就是一串带尖的骨头，所以这两个义项共用同一个形状。

branches.en: A book spine and a personal spine both hold something upright.
branches.cn: 书脊与人的骨气都在把东西撑直。

intro.en: Spine is a Latin sharp-point noun, and English builds spinal, spinous, spiny, and spineless around it.
intro.cn: spine 是拉丁语中表示「尖点」的名词，英语围绕它构成 spinal、spinous、spiny 与 spineless。

latinIntro.en: Latin spina means a thorn or prickle, and by extension the backbone that looks like a row of them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spina 意为刺、棘，并引申指像一排刺的脊柱。

items.example: Spina is the Latin source of spine.
items.exampleCN: spina 是 spine 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Anatomists still use spina dorsi for the backbone.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学至今仍用 spina dorsi 指背脊。

items.example: Old French espine carried the thorn sense.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 espine 保留了「刺」的含义。

items.example: Spine gathers all three senses in English.
items.exampleCN: spine 在英语里汇集了这三个义项。

items.example: Spinal means belonging to the backbone.
items.exampleCN: spinal 意为与脊柱有关的。

items.example: The suffix -al turns spine into spinal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 spine 变成 spinal。

items.meaning: full of spines or sharp points
items.example: Spinous describes a thorny surface.
items.exampleCN: spinous 形容多刺的表面。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms spinous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 spinous。

items.example: A spiny cactus guards its water.
items.exampleCN: 多刺的仙人掌守护着自己的水分。

items.example: The suffix -y forms spiny.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 spiny。

definition_en: a chemical made by a gland that travels in the blood and controls another part of the body
core_image: 一滴随血液赶路的化学信使，敲开远方器官的门
scene: 体检时，医生对着化验单上激素那一栏皱眉，说她的甲状腺工作得太慢。The doctor said her thyroid was not making enough hormone.
sceneCN: 这里 hormone 是「激素」（第 1 个义项：体内腺体分泌的化学信使）；句意：医生说她的甲状腺分泌的激素不够。

derivatives.zh: 激素的；由 hormone 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，指与激素有关的
以激素的方式；在激素方面；由 hormonal 加副词词尾 -ly 构成
激素原；由前缀 pro- 加 hormone 构成，指能转变成激素的前体物质

senses.title: A chemical messenger
senses.definition: a chemical made by a gland and carried in the blood to control another organ
senses.definitionCN: 由腺体制造、随血液运送、用来控制另一个器官的化学物质
senses.example: Insulin is a hormone that keeps blood sugar in range.
senses.exampleCN: 胰岛素是一种让血糖保持在正常范围的激素。
senses.why: Greek horman means to set in motion, so a hormone is the substance that sets an organ in motion.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 horman 意为「使行动」，所以激素就是让某个器官动起来的物质。

senses.title: A hormone medicine
senses.definition: a medicine that contains a natural hormone or copies its action
senses.definitionCN: 含有天然激素、或仿照天然激素起作用的药物
senses.example: The clinic gave her a hormone to correct the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所给她用了一种激素，补上缺少的量。
senses.why: Once scientists could isolate the messenger, they could also hand it over as a drug, so the word moved from the gland to the pharmacy.
senses.whyCN: 科学家一旦能把这种信使分离出来，也就能把它当药交到病人手里，于是这个词从腺体走进了药房。

senses.title: A plant growth substance
senses.definition: a chemical inside a plant that controls how the plant grows
senses.definitionCN: 植物体内控制生长方式的化学物质
senses.example: A plant hormone makes the stem bend toward the light.
senses.exampleCN: 一种植物激素让茎朝光弯过去。
senses.why: Plants steer their growth with chemical messengers too, so the driving image was extended from animals to plants.
senses.whyCN: 植物也用化学信使来操控生长，于是「驱动」的意象从动物延伸到了植物。

intro.en: Hormone goes back to Greek horman, to set in motion, and was taken up as a scientific term in 1905.
intro.cn: hormone 可追到希腊语 horman（使行动），一九〇五年被采用为科学术语。

items.en: Horme means an impulse or a sudden onset.
items.cn: horme 意为冲动、猛然起动。

items.en: Horman is the verb that means to set in motion or to urge on.
items.cn: horman 是动词，意为使行动、驱策。

items.en: Hormon is the participle that means setting in motion.
items.cn: hormon 是分词，意为「正在驱动的」。

items.en: Starling takes hormon as the name of a messenger carried in the blood.
items.cn: 斯塔林取 hormon 作为随血液传递的信使的名字。

items.en: Hormone enters English as a medical noun for that messenger.
items.cn: hormone 作为指这种信使的医学名词进入英语。

items.en: Modern English extends hormone to plant hormones and to hormone drugs.
items.cn: 现代英语把 hormone 扩展到植物激素与激素药物。

note.en: Hormone is a Greek driving word, and in meaning it sits near insulin, steroid, and pheromone in the field of body signals.
note.cn: hormone 是希腊语中表示「驱动」的词，在体内信号的义场里靠近 insulin、steroid 与 pheromone。

entries.definitionCN: 以激素的方式；在激素方面
不含添加激素的；由 hormone 与 free 组成的复合形容词

entries.definition: a hormone that lowers blood sugar
entries.definitionCN: 胰岛素；一种降低血糖的激素

entries.definition: a class of hormones built on four rings
entries.definitionCN: 类固醇；一类具有四环结构的激素

entries.definition: a chemical signal sent between animals
entries.definitionCN: 信息素；动物个体之间传递的化学信号

normalIntro.en: Hormone is built on the Greek idea of being driven: a gland sends a messenger, and an organ starts working.
normalIntro.cn: hormone 建立在希腊语「被驱动」的观念上：腺体派出信使，器官就开始工作。

normal.en: Horman in Greek means to urge on, so a hormone is the thing that urges the body.
normal.cn: 希腊语 horman 意为驱策，所以 hormone 就是驱策身体的那个东西。

normal.en: Growth hormone tells the body to build bone and muscle.
normal.cn: growth hormone 生长激素让身体长骨长肌。

normal.en: Hormone therapy replaces or blocks a natural hormone.
normal.cn: hormone therapy 激素疗法用来补充或阻断天然激素。

normal.en: Hormonal changes show the adjective at work: hormonal imbalance, hormonal shift.
normal.cn: hormonal changes 展示了形容词的用法：hormonal imbalance 激素失衡、hormonal shift 激素波动。

normal.en: Compare pheromone: a hormone works inside one body, a pheromone works between bodies.
normal.cn: 对比 pheromone：hormone 在同一个身体里起作用，pheromone 在个体之间起作用。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of liquid leaving a gland and riding the blood to a far organ.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴液体离开腺体，搭着血液赶往远处的器官。

abstract.en: Picture a small tablet standing in for a gland that has gone quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒小药片顶替一个已经沉默的腺体。

abstract.en: Picture a young shoot bending toward the window as a chemical tips it over.
abstract.cn: 想象一根幼苗朝窗口弯过去，像被某种化学物质轻轻推倒。

examples.en: Insulin is a hormone that lowers blood sugar after a meal.
examples.cn: 胰岛素是一种在饭后降低血糖的激素。

examples.en: She began hormone therapy after her thyroid surgery.
examples.cn: 甲状腺手术之后，她开始接受激素疗法。

examples.en: Plant hormones decide when a seed should start growing.
examples.cn: 植物激素决定一颗种子什么时候开始发芽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「荷尔蒙」——旧译正是 hormone 的音译，听起来像「合而蒙住」；这只是译音联想，与希腊语词源无关。

root: 希腊语 horman（驱动、使行动）→ 希腊语 hormon（正在驱动的）→ 一九〇五年斯塔林定为生理学术语 hormone → 现代英语 hormone；核心义是「驱动身体运转的那股力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Hormone begins as the body chemical that drives an organ, then covers the same substance given as medicine, and finally the plant substances that steer growth.
sensesIntro.cn: hormone 先指驱动器官的体内化学物质，再指同样成分的药物，最后指操控植物生长的物质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop of chemical riding the blood to start an engine in another organ.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴化学物质随血液赶路，去启动另一个器官的引擎。

branches.en: The body messenger is the first sense.
branches.cn: 体内的化学信使是第一个义项。

branches.en: The same substance given as a medicine is the second sense.
branches.cn: 把同样的物质当药使用，是第二个义项。

branches.en: Plants use their own messengers, which gives the third sense.
branches.cn: 植物有自己的信使，这带来第三个义项。

branches.en: Natural and prescribed hormones are the same molecules, and only the source differs.
branches.cn: 天然激素与处方激素是同一种分子，只是来源不同。

branches.en: Animal and plant hormones both carry orders that control growth or function.
branches.cn: 动物激素与植物激素都传递控制生长或功能的指令。

intro.en: Hormone is a Greek word for driving, and English builds hormonal, hormonally, prohormone, and hormone-free on it.
intro.cn: hormone 是希腊语中表示「驱动」的词，英语在它之上构成 hormonal、hormonally、prohormone 与 hormone-free。

latinIntro.en: Greek horman, to set in motion, gives the participle hormon, which scientific Latin kept as hormon.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 horman（使行动）给出分词 hormon，科学拉丁语沿用了 hormon 这一形式。

items.meaning: to set in motion, urge on
items.example: Horman gives hormone its driving image.
items.exampleCN: horman 为 hormone 提供了「驱动」的意象。

items.example: Horme names the first push.
items.exampleCN: horme 指最初的那一推。

items.example: Hormon is the participle behind the term.
items.exampleCN: hormon 是这个术语背后的分词。

items.example: Hormone names the messenger itself.
items.exampleCN: hormone 指这种信使本身。

items.example: Hormonal describes hormone effects.
items.exampleCN: hormonal 形容激素的作用。

items.example: The suffix -al forms hormonal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 hormonal。

items.example: Hormonally describes how a change happens.
items.exampleCN: hormonally 说明某种变化以激素方式发生。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms hormonally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 hormonally。

items.meaning: a substance that becomes a hormone
items.meaningCN: 激素原；能转变成激素的前体
items.example: A prohormone is one step before a hormone.
items.exampleCN: prohormone 是激素的前一步。

items.example: The prefix pro- forms prohormone.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 构成 prohormone。

items.example: Hormone-free labels appear on dairy products.
items.exampleCN: hormone-free 的标签出现在奶制品上。

latinEntries.example: New Latin kept hormon as the technical noun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 新拉丁语保留 hormon 作为术语名词。

definition_zh: 镇静剂；镇静的；使镇静的
definition_en: a medicine that calms a person, or having the power to calm
core_image: 一只手把躁动的身体轻轻按回椅子上
scene: 手术前一晚，护士端来一杯水和小小一片药，说这药会让人放松。The nurse said the sedative would help him relax before the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 sedative 是「镇静剂」（第 1 个义项：让人放松、平静下来的药）；句意：护士说这片镇静剂会帮他在手术前放松。

derivatives.zh: 镇静；由 sedative 的词干加名词词尾 -ation 构成，指用药后平静下来的状态
给某人用镇静剂；与 sedative 同出拉丁语 sedare，义为使人安定
已被施以镇静剂的；由 sedate 加 -ed 构成

senses.title: A calming medicine
senses.definition: a drug that makes a person calm, quiet, or sleepy
senses.definitionCN: 让人平静、安静或想睡的药物
senses.example: The nurse gave him a mild sedative before the scan.
senses.exampleCN: 做扫描之前，护士给他用了一点温和的镇静剂。
senses.why: Latin sedare means to settle or quiet something down, so a sedative is literally the thing that settles the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sedare 意为使平息、使安静，所以镇静剂字面上就是让身体安定下来的东西。

senses.title: Calming in effect
senses.definition: having the effect of making someone calmer
senses.definitionCN: 具有让人变得更平静的效果
senses.example: The drug has a sedative effect and can make you drowsy.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药有镇静作用，会让人昏昏欲睡。
senses.why: Latin sedativus was an adjective meaning calming, so the same form kept its adjective sense beside the noun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sedativus 本就是形容词，意为「能平息的」，所以这个词在名词之外一直保留着形容词义。

senses.title: Something that soothes
senses.definition: anything that quiets the mind, such as a place, a sound, or an activity
senses.definitionCN: 任何能让心绪平静下来的东西，如一个地方、一种声音或一项活动
senses.example: For him, the long walk by the river was a sedative.
senses.exampleCN: 对他来说，沿河的长距离散步就是一剂镇静药。
senses.why: From a drug that settles the nerves, the word spreads to anything that presses the noise of the mind down.
senses.whyCN: 从让神经安定下来的药物出发，这个词扩展到任何能把脑子里的嘈杂压下去的东西。

intro.en: Sedative comes from Latin sedare, to settle or calm, a verb built on sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: sedative 来自拉丁语 sedare（使平息、使安静），这个词又建立在 sedere（坐）之上。

items.en: Sedere means to sit or to stay seated.
Sedare is a frequentative of sedere and means to settle or calm something down.
items.cn: sedare 是 sedere 的反复动词，意为使某物安定、平息。

items.en: Sedativus is the adjective that means calming or soothing.
items.cn: sedativus 是形容词，意为能平息的、能安抚的。

items.en: Sedative enters medical English as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: sedative 在十七世纪作为形容词和名词一起进入医学英语。

items.en: Modern English uses sedative for the drug and for any calming influence.
items.cn: 现代英语的 sedative 既指药物，也指任何起安抚作用的影响。

note.en: Sedative belongs to a Latin family about sitting down, and in meaning it stands near tranquilizer, hypnotic, and calmative.
note.cn: sedative 属于拉丁语中表示「坐定」的词族，在意义上靠近 tranquilizer、hypnotic 与 calmative。

entries.definition: the state of being calmed by a drug
entries.definitionCN: 镇静状态；用药后平静下来的状态

entries.definition: to calm a person with a drug
entries.definitionCN: 给某人用镇静剂使其安定
已被施以镇静剂的；处于药物镇静状态的
安定药；减轻焦虑的药物

entries.definition: a drug that brings on sleep
entries.definitionCN: 催眠药；促使人入睡的药物
温和的镇静剂；起安抚作用的药物

normalIntro.en: Sedative is built on the Latin picture of sitting down: sedare makes something settle, and a sedative settles the nerves.
normalIntro.cn: sedative 建立在拉丁语「坐下来」的画面上：sedare 让某物安定，镇静剂让神经安定。

normal.en: The root sed- comes from sedere, to sit, and sedare means to make something sit still.
normal.cn: 词干 sed- 来自 sedere（坐），sedare 意为让某物坐着不动。

normal.en: A mild sedative is often given before a scan or a small procedure.
normal.cn: mild sedative 温和的镇静剂常在扫描或小手术前使用。

normal.en: A sedative effect is a common side effect of some allergy drugs.
normal.cn: sedative effect 镇静作用是一些抗过敏药常见的副作用。

normal.en: Compare sleeping pill: a sedative quiets the nerves, while a sleeping pill aims at sleep itself.
normal.cn: 对比 sleeping pill：sedative 主要让神经安静，sleeping pill 直接冲着睡眠去。

normal.en: The family stays together: sedate, sedation, sedated, and sedative all share the settling idea.
normal.cn: 这一族词连在一起：sedate、sedation、sedated 与 sedative 都共享「安定」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a restless animal held gently until it sits down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只躁动的小动物被人轻轻按住，慢慢坐了下来。

abstract.en: Picture a warm bowl of soup going down and the shoulders dropping.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗热汤下肚，肩膀一点点松下来。

abstract.en: Picture rain sound flattening the noisy thoughts in a head.
abstract.cn: 想象雨声把脑子里吵闹的念头一层层压平。

examples.en: The dentist gave her a mild sedative before the extraction.
examples.cn: 拔牙之前，牙医给她用了一点温和的镇静剂。

examples.en: This medicine has a sedative effect and can make you drowsy.
examples.cn: 这种药有镇静作用，会让人昏昏欲睡。

examples.en: She took a sedative and slept through the night.
examples.cn: 她服了一剂镇静药，一觉睡到天亮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前半截读起来像「睡得」——用了镇静剂就「睡得」安稳；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语 sedare 无关。

root: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）→ 拉丁语 sedare（使坐下、使平息）→ 拉丁语 sedativus（能平息的）→ 英语 sedative；核心义是「把躁动按下去，让它坐定」。

sensesIntro.en: Sedative starts as the drug that settles the body, keeps the adjective sense of calming, and then widens to anything that soothes the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: sedative 先指让身体安定下来的药物，同时保留「使平息」的形容词义，最后扩展到任何能安抚心绪的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a restless body gently back into a chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把躁动的身体轻轻按回椅子上。

branches.en: The calming drug is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 让人平静的药物是日常义项。

branches.en: The calming quality is the adjective sense.
branches.cn: 具有平息作用，是形容词义项。

branches.en: Anything that quiets the mind is the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 任何让心绪安静下来的事物，是引申义项。

branches.en: The drug and its effect are named by the same form.
branches.cn: 药物与它的作用由同一个词形来指称。

branches.en: Both quiet the mind, one through chemistry and one through a place or a sound.
branches.cn: 两者都让心绪安静，只是一个靠药物，一个靠某个地方或某种声音。

intro.en: Sedative is a Latin settling word, and English builds sedate, sedation, and sedated around it.
intro.cn: sedative 是拉丁语中表示「使安定」的词，英语围绕它构成 sedate、sedation 与 sedated。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit, sedare means to settle, and sedativus means calming.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，sedare 意为使平息，sedativus 意为能平息的。

items.example: Sedere gives the picture of sitting down.
items.exampleCN: sedere 提供「坐下来」的画面。

items.example: Sedare turns sitting into settling.
items.exampleCN: sedare 把「坐」变成「使安定」。

items.example: Sedativus is the adjective that reaches English.
items.exampleCN: sedativus 是进入英语的那个形容词。

items.example: Sedative names the medicine itself.
items.exampleCN: sedative 指这种药物本身。

items.meaning: to calm someone with a drug
items.example: Doctors sedate a patient before some procedures.
items.exampleCN: 医生在某些操作前会给病人用镇静剂。

items.meaning: the state of being calmed by drugs
items.example: Sedation keeps the patient quiet and still.
items.exampleCN: sedation 让病人安静不动。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms sedation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 sedation。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ive forms sedative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 sedative。

items.example: A sedated patient sleeps through the test.
items.exampleCN: 被镇静的病人会在检查中睡着。

items.example: A calmative herb can ease mild nerves.
items.exampleCN: 有镇静作用的草药能缓解轻度的紧张。
